chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever finds something, it is for him; so let him enjoy it until its seeker comes to him. So when its seeker comes, he should return it to him.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on keeping found property?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the temporary custodial nature of found property, distinguishing between mere possession for use and permanent ownership. It underscores the ethical obligation in Shia jurisprudence to maintain the item until the rightful owner is identified, reflecting the principle of preserving trust (amanah) in daily transactions. The ruling emphasizes that the finder's right is provisional, contingent upon the eventual restitution to the original owner.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who finds anything, so it is for him. So let him enjoy with it until its seeker comes along. So when its seeker comes along, he should return it to him’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever finds something it is for him to benefit thereby until the owner comes. He then must give it to the owner.” (Consult Fatwa also.)
